newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Upstart Dutch rail firm goes on the offensive.
newsitem.headline: Upstart Dutch rail firm goes on the offensive.

text.p: A small Dutch rail company launched a direct attack on the monopoly of state-owned Dutch Railways (NS) on Tuesday by revealing plans to start five new train services next year in the urban heart of the Netherlands.

Lovers Rail, set up by a canal boat cruise firm, began the first private service on the Dutch rail network in August with an express beach service linking Amsterdam to the North Sea coast with trains running over a disused stretch of track.
By contrast the new services would run over mainline routes between the major cities of Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht and would also take in Schiphol Airport and Haarlem.
Lovers said the new services would target commuters and tourists and would radically alter conventional fare structures.
"Some passengers don't want to sit down during a short train ride. Less service means that they also have to pay less," said Peter Sul, managing director of Lovers Rail.
Sul said passengers would also be able to reserve a seat, a facility not available on Dutch Railways' domestic services.
The transport ministry confirmed it had received Lovers' applications but could not say whether it would grant the firm a licence to start the services next year.
"We have to look at the proposals and see whether they merit approval," a spokeswoman said.

Dutch Railways was not available for comment, but has previously said that Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma should introduce competition by offering complete tracks to new companies rather than designated time slots on selected routes.

"She should not allow newcomers to pick the cherries and leave Dutch Railways to run the less attractive lines," spokesman Tijs Manten said earlier this month. "Competition is not a goal in itself. Improving services is the key," he added.
Dutch Railways currently uses profits it makes on its intercity services to cover losses on local services.
Minister Jorritsma is due to present guidelines for competition in passenger train traffic later this year.
Lovers plans half-hourly commuter trains between Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Utrecht from June 1997 and a similar commuter service between Amsterdam and the dormitory town of Hilversum.
It also plans hourly services to a large recreation and leisure area outside Amsterdam and an express service to the Keukenhof floral park from next spring.
